**Finding submitted: deviation on Section 6.1 (p0037), redlined to the fallback position.**

**What I found**

Section 6.1 is the only non-compete/field-of-use restriction binding our client (the Company). It fails the fallback on three material terms:

| Fallback element | Status in document |
|---|---|
| Named competing product only | **Fails** — reaches "products substantially similar to Deerskin Products" and, "without limitation," Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled "and companies similar to" them: the undefined scope the playbook treats as walk-away |
| During the term only | **Met** — Section 10.7 limits survival to §§ 6.3, 7, 9 and 10, so 6.1 has no post-term tail |
| No longer than 12 months | **Fails** — Section 4.1 auto-renews the term annually, so "during the term" can run indefinitely |
| Internal development carve-out | **Fails** — only exception is the narrow closeout-merchandise site in 6.2; § 9(b) Globix language is transitional |
| Acquisitions carve-out | **Fails** — absent |

**Direction check:** Section 6.3 imposes a two-year post-term restriction on HDI, and Section 6.2 plus § 9(b) are carve-outs in our favour — all benefit us, so none are flagged.

**Target chosen:** fallback rather than preferred deletion, because HDI funds all Site development and hosting and is paid solely from Net Sales on the Site, so its exclusivity is the core economics of the bargain. One surgical replace (60 words for 60) narrows scope to the named Deerskin Products, adds "in no event for more than twelve (12) months," and adds a parenthetical carve-out for our internal development and acquisitions — leaving HDI's "Deerskin" brand exclusivity for the Site untouched.
